questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Benin?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Benin article.

questions.proof: The capital of Benin is Porto-Novo.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Benin?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Benin on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Benin article.

questions.proof: Benin is bordered by Togo to the west, Burkina Faso and Niger to the north, Nigeria to the east, and the Bight of Benin to the south.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Benin?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Benin article.

questions.proof: Because Benin was colonized by France and is still close to it, the official language of Benin is French.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The current Republic of Benin was formed in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Benin article.

questions.proof: The current Republic of Benin was formed in 1991.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1960, Dahomey gained official independence from _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “independence”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Benin article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In 1960, Dahomey gained official independence from France.
